messages.subject: Combining multiple datasets
messages.body_plain:
Greetings and salutations,

I am looking to combine multiple .imzML for tumor vs normal analysis but have hit a bit of a snag as pixel across multiple sets have the same coordinates, this seems to prohibit combining them into a single MSImageSet. Is there a workaround for this?

Thanking you in advance

-Dmitri

messages.subject: Re: Combining multiple datasets
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dmitri,

Firstly, there is no "msset_t" defined in your code. I assume this is just a typo.

Can you check levels(msset_n$sample) for both datasets? My first guess would be that the sample names are the same in both datasets, but readImzML should set the sample names to be the same as the file names, so they should be different already.

Then check if there are duplicated coordinates in either dataset:

any(duplicated(coord(msset_n)))

If this is TRUE, then try dropping the pixels from duplicated coordinates:

msset_n <- msset_n[,!duplicated(coord(msset_n))]

Then try combining them.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Combining multiple datasets
messages.body_plain:
Usually they shouldn't have duplicate coordinates. If you didn't collect the data yourself, then I would ask whoever did.

One typical reason is if it's a 3D experiment or a multimodal experiment that has been co-registered, then the x, y, z, coordinates may be spatially transformed and be non-integer. In this case, they end up being rounded to the nearest gridded integer, which may result in duplicate coordinates.

If you do readImzML with as="MSImagingExperiment", the new classes and methods should handle this a little more elegantly, but some methods for these newer classes are still under development.

-Kylie

Hi team,

Have a question about the supervised analysis example, we have a similar scenario however the tumour and normal samples are on separate .imzML files. So when combining them and using the cvApply function each sample will only have one of the two response variables (i.e. all the pixels are either tumour or normal) which I would assume is problematic (and results with an error below when the summary() function is applied to the object). Is this a correct assumption? If so is there an alternative without having to try and re-export imzML files containing both tumour/normal one the one image?

As always, thanking you in advance!

-Dmitri

The default is to use separate runs as the CV folds, but this may not make sense for every dataset. Create a pixelData variable that defines the folds as you like (a factor or character vector with different levels for each fold, with length equal to the total number of spectra, where the elements define which fold each spectrum belongs to), and provide this as the argument to the .fold argument in cvApply.

(I’m on mobile right now and can’t give a more detailed example. Hopefully this helps.)

-Kylie

But I need to extract the mean spectra of a chosen ROI to a seperated data frame. I know how to plot the mean spectra, but how I can extract the data? Perhaps it's useful to mention, that my imzML-datasets are all processed.

dataset_df <-featureApply(dataset,.fun=myfun)

messages.subject: Re: BiocParallel errors while normalizing
messages.body_plain: readonly() is from the “matter” package that Cardinal uses as a backend for file-based matrices. It is only used if the data is read with “attach.only=TRUE”.
